# Recorded dataset fixtures

Captured **2026-09-03** from the live upstreams. These files are recorded
payloads, not generated ones: every value is verbatim as the upstream served
it, and the only thing this repository decided is which providers to keep. A
fixture generated by this framework would test the framework against itself
and could never disagree with it, which is the whole point of recording.

| file | upstream | fetched |
|---|---|---|
| `models_dev_2026-09-03.json` | `https://models.dev/api.json` | HTTP 200, 4,461,205 bytes |
| `litellm_2026-09-03.json` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json` | HTTP 200, 2,090,796 bytes |

## What the slice is

Each file keeps the **complete** record set for every upstream provider named
in `mapping.py`, and drops the rest. Nothing inside a kept provider is
filtered, so within a mapped provider family the fixture is the whole upstream
truth and the measured match rate is a real measurement rather than an
artefact of selection. Selecting the records that happen to match would make
the match rate 100% by construction and the floor test meaningless.

- `models_dev_2026-09-03.json`: 14 providers, 543 models (of 213 providers,
  7,520 models upstream).
- `litellm_2026-09-03.json`: 1,447 entries (of 3,518 upstream).

Verified at capture time: comparing the catalog against these slices produces
byte-identical findings and byte-identical coverage to comparing it against the
two full payloads.

## Re-capturing

```bash
curl -sSL https://models.dev/api.json -o /tmp/modelsdev.json
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json \
     -o /tmp/litellm.json
```

```python
import json
from bili.iris.config.catalog_divergence.mapping import (
    LITELLM_PROVIDERS, MODELS_DEV_PROVIDERS)

md = json.load(open("/tmp/modelsdev.json"))
ll = json.load(open("/tmp/litellm.json"))
md_ids = {p for ids in MODELS_DEV_PROVIDERS.values() for p in ids}
ll_ids = {p for ids in LITELLM_PROVIDERS.values() for p in ids}

json.dump({k: md[k] for k in sorted(md_ids) if k in md},
          open("models_dev_<YYYY-MM-DD>.json", "w"), indent=1, sort_keys=True)
json.dump({k: v for k, v in ll.items()
           if isinstance(v, dict) and v.get("litellm_provider") in ll_ids},
          open("litellm_<YYYY-MM-DD>.json", "w"), indent=1, sort_keys=True)
```

Re-capturing under a new date will move the match-rate floors and the
finding counts the tests pin. That is the point: those tests measure *this*
repository against *these* recorded bytes, and the scheduled job is what
measures it against whatever the upstreams say today. Update the floors
deliberately, in the same change, with the new numbers.

These fixtures are test data and are excluded from the built distribution:
`find_packages(exclude=["*.tests", "*.tests.*", ...])` in `setup.py` drops the
test packages, and `MANIFEST.in` names only the runtime data directories.
